subject: Tyska
title: Reading comprehension: a message to a friend
sourceSummary: A text message about weekend plans, with questions about details, times, and feelings.

questions.prompt:
Read the message: "Hallo, Marta! Am Samstag gehe ich mit meinem Bruder ins Kino. Der Film beginnt um sieben Uhr. Willst du mitkommen?"

What is the person going to do on Saturday?
questions.explanation: "Ich gehe ins Kino" means "I'm going to the movies".

questions.prompt: Same message. What time does the movie start?
questions.opener: "Um sieben Uhr" — look for the time.
questions.explanation: "Der Film beginnt um sieben Uhr" means "the movie starts at seven o'clock".

questions.prompt: Same message. What does the person ask Marta?
questions.opener: The last sentence is a question.
choices: If she wants to see a different movie
If she wants to come along
If she's seen the movie before
questions.explanation: "Willst du mitkommen?" means "do you want to come along?".

questions.prompt:
Marta's reply: "Klar, gerne! Ich liebe Abenteuerfilme. Um wie viel Uhr treffen wir uns?"

What does Marta think of adventure movies?
questions.explanation: "Ich liebe Abenteuerfilme" means "I love adventure movies".

questions.prompt: Same reply. What does Marta ask at the end?
questions.opener: "Um wie viel Uhr...?" asks about time, "treffen wir uns" means "we meet".
questions.explanation: "Um wie viel Uhr treffen wir uns?" means "what time should we meet?".

questions.prompt: Who suggests going to the movies — the person who writes first, or Marta? Answer with "the person who writes first".
Write a short German sentence (3–5 words) that answers: "Welche Filme mag Marta?" (Which movies does Marta like?)
questions.opener: The answer is in Marta's own reply.
steps: Find the sentence in the text: "Ich liebe Abenteuerfilme."
Swap "ich" for "sie" since the question is about Marta (she), not "I".

questions.prompt: Which phrases are good to recognize in a German text message about plans?
questions.opener: Everyday phrases for suggesting, agreeing, and setting a time.
questions.answer: Suggesting: Willst du mitkommen? = Do you want to come along? · ich gehe... = I'm going... Agreeing: Klar, gerne! = Sure, gladly! · Ich liebe... = I love... Setting a time: Um wie viel Uhr treffen wir uns? = What time should we meet? · beginnt um... = starts at... Feelings: ich mag = I like · ich liebe = I love (stronger) · ich mag ... nicht = I don't like.

questions.prompt:
Read the message: "Liebe Anna, am Sonntag feiere ich meinen Geburtstag. Die Party beginnt um vier Uhr bei mir zu Hause. Kannst du kommen? Bring gern deine Schwester mit!"

What is the person celebrating on Sunday?
questions.explanation: "Ich feiere meinen Geburtstag" means "I'm celebrating my birthday".

questions.prompt: Same message. What time does the party start?
questions.opener: "Um vier Uhr" — look for the time.
questions.explanation: "Die Party beginnt um vier Uhr" means "the party starts at four o'clock".

questions.prompt: Same message. Who is Anna welcome to bring along?
questions.opener: Look for the last sentence: "Bring gern deine...".
questions.explanation: "Bring gern deine Schwester mit!" means "feel free to bring your sister along!".

questions.prompt:
Anna's reply: "Hallo! Danke für die Einladung. Ich komme gern, aber meine Schwester kann leider nicht kommen — sie ist krank. Was soll ich mitbringen?"

Can Anna's sister come to the party?
questions.opener: Look for the sentence about the sister.
questions.explanation: "Meine Schwester kann leider nicht kommen — sie ist krank" means "my sister unfortunately can't come — she's sick".

questions.prompt: Same reply. What does Anna ask in the last sentence?
questions.opener: "Was soll ich mitbringen?" — look for the question word "was".
questions.explanation: "Was soll ich mitbringen?" means "what should I bring?".

questions.prompt: Same reply. What does Anna thank for?
questions.explanation: "Danke für die Einladung" means "thanks for the invitation".

questions.prompt: Same reply. Is Anna coming to the party?
choices: She asks for a different day
questions.explanation: "Ich komme gern" means "I'd love to come".
